rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for a plant producing or opening its flowers.

example.english: This orchid has finally begun to bloom.
example.jyutping: ni1 pun4 laan4 faa1 zung1 jyu1 hoi1 faa1 laa3

rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for a blossom or flower.

example.english: This flower is in full bloom.
example.jyutping: ni1 do2 faa1 hoi1 dak1 hou2 leng3

rows.note: Use this for the period or state of youth, freshness, and vitality rather than for a literal flower.

example.english: Once the bloom of youth is gone, it never comes back.
example.jyutping: cing1 ceon1 jat1 heoi3 zau6 m4 faan1 gaa3 laa3

rows.note: Use this when “bloom” means the flowering season or period when plants have flowers open.

example.english: The bloom period of this orchid is quite long.
example.jyutping: ni1 zung2 laan4 faa1 ge3 faa1 kei4 hou2 coeng4

rows.note: Use this when something gradually spreads across an area, such as shadows, fire, or disease.

example.english: The shadows slowly bloom across the whole room.
example.traditional: 陰影慢慢蔓延到成間屋。
example.jyutping: jam1 jing2 maan6 maan6 maan6 jin4 dou3 seng4 gaan1 uk1

rows.note: Use this for a person, business, or place that is growing and doing well rather than for literal flowers.

example.english: This little shop continues to bloom, and business keeps getting better.
example.traditional: 呢間小店近年發展得好，生意越做越旺。
example.jyutping: ni1 gaan1 siu2 dim3 gan6 nin4 faat3 zin2 dak1 hou2 sang1 ji3 jyut6 zou6 jyut6 wong6

rows.note: Use this for a rosy flush or glow on someone's cheeks; it is more literary than everyday 面紅.

example.english: A rosy bloom appeared on their cheeks.
example.jyutping: keoi5 min6 soeng6 faan6 hei2 jat1 mut3 hung4 wan4
